about: Neutrality guard lexicon for generated Filing Footnote summaries. Read by backend/app/llm/neutrality_guard.py. Every rule has an id; severity 'fail' blocks a line, 'warn' only reports it. Match modes: 'substring' finds the term anywhere (Korean); 'word' needs word boundaries, case-insensitive, spaces match any whitespace (English); 'inflected_word' is 'word' plus English verb and noun endings (-s, -es, -ed, -ing, -ly, -ness, -en, -less; a final e is dropped before -ing/-ed/-y; a final consonant + y becomes -ies/-ied), and comparative -er/-est only for terms in 'adjectives'. 'phrases' are matched as written, without endings (in Korean a space matches an optional space); 'patterns' are regular expressions. A hit that lies wholly inside an 'allow' phrase or an 'allow_patterns' regular expression is ignored; in Korean allow phrases a space matches an optional space (장내 매수 also covers 장내매수). Company names the caller passes are also exempt from N2 (not from N1). 'narrowed' records every listed word that no longer matches as a bare word, with the reason; 'added' records everything beyond the M5 plan list.

rules.title: No digits
rules.note: Implemented in code by reuse: NFKC normalisation then any \d (neutrality_guard._ANY_DIGIT_RE), plus spelled financial numbers (number_guard._SPELLED_FINANCIAL_RE, _SPELLED_PREFIX_RE, _KOREAN_SPELLED_RE), plus the ko/en lists below. English counts spelled without a unit or currency ('three quarters') are not caught. Known limitation: a company name with a digit (3M) always fails; the pipeline must have the model write 회사/The company. 'labels' (D111) are the only digits and ordinals that may pass, and only when the caller passes the source and the source holds the same label.
rules.labels_note: D111, owner decision 2026-11-28. A label names something; it is not a figure. Each pattern's 'value' group is the label's key: the digits, a spelled ordinal as its digit (third -> 3), a form name in capitals. A line's label is exempt from N1 only when the same kind and key occur in the source text (either language, so 'third quarter' matches 3분기 and '2026 회계연도' matches 'fiscal 2026'). Years: four digits from 1900 to 2099 before 년 (not 년간 or 년 동안), 회계연도 or 사업연도, or after fiscal, fiscal year or FY. Quarters are an allow-list of shapes: 1분기 to 4분기 written without a space and followed by a noun from a closed list (실적, 잠정, 영업실적, 보고서, 결산, 배당, 배당금, 매출, 매출액, 영업이익, 순이익, 중, 말, 초) with an optional particle, or by one of 에, 에는, 에도, 의, 부터, 까지, 는, 은, or by punctuation or the end of the line; in each shape no count or duration word may follow (연속, 이상, 이하, 넘게, 내내, 동안, 합산, 만에, 례, 째, 씩, 걸쳐, 나눠). In English, first to fourth quarter followed by (of) (fiscal (year)) a year, by results, report, earnings or dividend(s), or by punctuation or the end of the line, so the third quarter in a row stays banned; halves (상반기, first half) and spelled Korean quarters (삼분기) stay banned. Rounds are an allow-list too: N차, or a list N차와 M차 (와, 과, 및 or a comma), directly before a noun from a closed list (발행가액, 발행가, 발행, 공시, 납입, 청약, 입찰, 매각, 정정, 모집) with an optional particle and no count word after it, so 4차 연속, 3차 이상, 2차 례, 2차전지, 3차원, 차이, the lanes 4차로, 2차례, 2차에 걸쳐 and 3차에 나눠 stay banned. Plants: one digit directly before 공장 (2 공장 reads as a count), or Plant N. Forms: the SEC form names listed, with an optional /A. Amounts, percentages, prices, counts and durations (6개월, six months) stay banned; a bare English year (in 2026) stays banned.

added.term: Korean numeral + 만/억/조/천/백, optional space, then 원/달러/퍼센트/% (천억 원, 삼조 원) or 주 (삼백만 주)
added.reason: number_guard._KOREAN_SPELLED_RE needs the unit and 원 joined; spaced amounts passed. Defined in neutrality_guard.py, number_guard.py unchanged. 원 followed by 칙/가/본/료/화/래/인/격/자/천 is a separate word (원칙, 원가) and does not count.

added.term: numeral + 만/억/조/천 before 규모/어치/명/건/개/주/원/달러 (일조 규모)
added.reason: bare spelled magnitude used as an amount

added.term: $, €, £ or ₩ followed by a spelled number ($two billion)
added.reason: _CURRENCY_PREFIX_RE needs digits; _SPELLED_PREFIX_RE needs a currency code

added.term: ko: 절반, 삼분기, 두 배, native count 한/두/세/네 + 곳/명/건/개/배; en: doubled
added.reason: owner-approved 2026-11-17

added.term: ko: 일분기, 이분기, 사분기 (no space; 이 분기 means this quarter), 상반기, 하반기; en: first/second/third/fourth + quarter/half
added.reason: owner-approved 2026-11-18 (D74): the pilot wrote fourth quarter and third quarter

ko.note: Native counts: the counter must stand alone or take a particle, so 한 개발, 두 배당, 세 건물 are clear; a syllable before 한/두/세/네 (달성한, 공시한) also clears it.
No allow list. 우려 and 충격 have no innocent compound likely in a filing summary; a filing's own use of 우려 is still a judgement word and is not quoted.

added.term: 껑충, 곤두박질, 깜짝, 급증, 급감, 놀라운, 눈부신, 부진; phrase 전망이 밝
added.reason: owner-approved 2026-11-17

en.note: Endings catch surged, soaring, strongly, weaker, weakest, weakness, flawless. Comparative -er/-est is applied only to adjectives, because -er on a verb makes a different word (booster, jumper). Word boundaries keep 'surgery' and 'Armstrong' clear. Company names passed by the caller (Boost Mobile, Jump Trading) are exempt.

added.term: adjectives: strong, weak
added.reason: Limits -er/-est to the two adjectives so 'booster' passes and 'weakest' fails.

added.term: rally, plummet, huge, remarkable, robust, stellar, blowout, spike (with endings)
added.reason: owner-approved 2026-11-17

added.term: phrases only: tanked, rocketed, solid results
added.reason: owner-approved 2026-11-17; bare tank, rocket and solid have factual senses (storage tank, rocket launch, solid-state)

dated_future.note: D111, coordinator decision 2026-11-28: a source-held year or quarter label must not enable a dated forecast. On a line where a year or quarter label passed N1 (the source holds it), these regular expressions (English case-insensitive) also fail N3: future, plan and target forms. Lines without such a label are unchanged; the general question of a bare 'will' is out of scope. The summary prompt does not read this list.

ko.note: after_rieul: any syllable ending in ㄹ (할, 될, 오를, 늘어날), an optional space, then the word; this is the plan's '~ㄹ 전망'. Past forms (한 것으로, 보인) do not match. 보인다 also blocks the literal sense 'shows'; write 보여 줬다고 instead. plan_gated: 예정/계획 used as a predicate must be the quoted form 예정이라고/계획이라고 in a line that passes N4. Nouns from the forms (예정일, 예정금액, 보유처분계획을) and the adnominal 예정인 before a noun (소각 예정인 주식 수) are not gated.

added.term: 전망돼요, 전망이다, 전망입니다, 전망됩니다, 예상됩니다, 기대됩니다, 보입니다
added.reason: Other endings of the listed words; the plan named the 해요체 forms only.

added.term: plan_gated forms 이에요/이예요/이다/입니다/이며/이고/이었/이라고/이래요/임/으로 after 예정 or 계획
added.reason: The plan names only the allowed forms; these are the predicate forms that must be rewritten as 예정이라고/계획이라고.

added.term: after_rieul 것이, 거예요, 거에요, 겁니다 (~ㄹ 것이다/거예요), 듯 (~ㄹ 듯), 것 같 (~ㄹ 것 같); phrases 가능성이 있, 리라
added.reason: owner-approved 2026-11-17

narrowed.now_matches: any ㄹ-final syllable + 전망, except inside 매출 전망
narrowed.reason: 매출 (revenue) ends in ㄹ, so '회사는 매출 전망을 공시했어요', a company-stated outlook, would fail. Only that noun is allow-listed.

en.note: 'could' fails everywhere, including inside quotation marks: summaries do not quote risk factors. 'will' on its own is not listed and does not fail; owner to decide. plan_gated: a stated plan may appear only as 'plans to' / 'intends to' in a line that passes N4. After a/an/the/its/their the word is a noun ('a plan to repurchase shares') and is not gated.

added.term: are expected to, are likely to, analyst
added.reason: Plural and singular forms of listed phrases.

added.term: expects to
added.reason: A company forecast, not a stated plan; the plan allows 'plans to' and 'intends to' only.

added.term: plan_gated: plan(s|ned|ning), intend(s|ed|ing), aim(s|ed|ing) + to
added.reason: The plan names only the allowed forms; these are the other plan verbs that must be rewritten as 'plans to'/'intends to'.

added.term: might, poised, on track; patterns expect* (expects, expected, expecting, expectation(s)), anticipat*, forecast*
added.reason: owner-approved 2026-11-17; 'plans to' and 'intends to' stay allowed

ko.note: Every line ends with an ending (trailing spaces and . ! ? ignored). Line one starts with 회사는 or a company name followed by one of name_particles (증권회사는, 자회사는 fail). Any line that starts with a third-party subject (optionally + 들, then a third_party_particle) fails. report_endings (D111): line one of a clarification filing (title starting 풍문또는보도에대한해명, after an optional [기재정정]-style tag) may also end in 해명했어요, and line one of an inquiry answer (title starting 조회공시요구, an optional bracket, 에대한답변) in 답변했어요 or 조회공시 요구를 받았어요 (a space matches an optional space). They need the caller to pass the filing's title; lines two and three keep the five endings.

added.term: name_particles: 은, 는, 이, 가
added.reason: The plan says 'the company name'; these are the subject and topic particles that make it the subject.

added.term: third_party_subjects: 애널리스트, 증권가, 투자자, 시장, 업계, 전문가 (+들, + 은/는/이/가/에서는/에선)
added.reason: Lines two and three may omit the subject, but an explicit third-party subject attributes the line to someone other than the company.

en.note: Leading markdown markers (# > * + -) are skipped before the start check; N6 reports them. Every line starts with '<subject> [suffix] [adverb] <verb>', where subject is 'The company' or a company name the caller passes. Callers pass every name form they want accepted (for example both 'Apple' and 'Apple Inc.'). 'Apple's board said', 'It said', 'Investors said the company reported' fail.

added.term: adverbs: also, further, separately, previously
added.reason: Lets 'The company also said' pass; the plan names no adverbs.

added.term: name_suffixes: Inc., Corp., Co., Corporation, Incorporated
added.reason: Lets 'Apple Inc. said' pass when the caller passes only 'Apple'.

rules.title: Official source link
rules.note: Only check_source_url here; the exporter (M8) enforces it per summary.

rules.title: Shape
rules.note: Lengths count Unicode code points after NFKC. Fullwidth ！ becomes ! under NFKC.

narrowed.now_matches: every use except the filing's own terms in allow
narrowed.reason: Filings use them for the method, party or instrument: 장내 매수 (on-market purchase, the buyback filing's 취득방법), 매도 주문수량 한도, 공개매수 (tender offer), 주식매수선택권 (stock options), 주식매수청구권 (appraisal right), 매도가능 (available-for-sale), 매수인/매도인 (buyer/seller in a contract). Bare 매수/매도 still fail; summaries write 취득/처분 for the company's own trades.
사외이사후보추천위원회 is a board committee's legal name. 이사회가 추천한 후보 still fails; write 이사회가 정한 후보.

added.term: allow: 매수인, 매도인, spaced 매수 청구권/매수 선택권/매도 청구권
added.reason: Contract parties and the spaced spelling of the legal rights.

added.term: 저평가, 고평가; phrases 살 때, 투자할 만, 주목할 만
added.reason: owner-approved 2026-11-17

added.term: phrases only: 매수 기회, 투자 기회
added.reason: owner-approved 2026-11-17; bare 기회 is generic (사업 기회)

added.term: allow: 강제 매수
added.reason: D111, owner decision 2026-11-28: 강제매수 is the legal term for a compulsory acquisition of minority shares (a squeeze-out), like 공개매수.

added.term: allow_patterns: 채권/사채/노트 + 을/를 + optional 인수단/인수인/주관사/(기관)투자자(들) + 에/에게 + 매도 before 하기로, 했다/했어요/했고/했으며/했습니다, 할 예정 or 할 계획
added.reason: D111, owner decision 2026-11-28: the company selling the notes it issues (채권을 인수단에 매도하기로 합의했어요) is a fact. Shares stay out: the company's own share trades are written 취득/처분 (자기주식을 매도 still fails), as is any other form (매도하세요, 매도해야, 매도할 때, 매도하는 것이, 매도한다면) and any other buyer word (유망기업에 매도 keeps 유망 banned).

allow: board of directors recommended that shareholders vote
board of directors recommends that shareholders vote

narrowed.reason: 'The company said it decided to buy back its own shares' is a buyback fact.
'The company said it sells products' and 'agreed to sell its stake' are facts.
'holding company', 'holds shares', 'holders of the notes', 'placed a hold on the program' are facts; word boundaries alone already keep 'shareholders' and 'threshold' clear.

narrowed.now_matches: every inflection except a board's vote recommendation ('board recommended that shareholders vote', 'board recommends a vote')
narrowed.reason: A proxy or 5.07 filing states the board's voting recommendation. The allow phrase includes the vote, so 'the board recommends buying the stock' still fails.

added.term: recommends, recommended, recommending, recommendation, recommendations
added.reason: Inflections of 'recommend', listed because this rule uses word match.

added.term: patterns 'buying/selling (the/its/more) stock/shares' and 'investor(s) (should/to) buy/sell/hold'
added.reason: Catch advice that sits next to a board recommendation.

added.term: worth a look, good time to invest, attractive valuation, buying opportunity, must-buy, cheap
added.reason: owner-approved 2026-11-17

rules.title: Language
rules.note: Korean lines contain Hangul; English lines contain none.

ko.note: Allow entries are filing terms (largest shareholder, chief officer titles), so they produce no warning.

added.term: allow: 최대주주, 최고경영자, 최고재무책임자, 최고운영책임자, 최고기술책임자
added.reason: Filing terms that contain 최대/최고 with no intensity meaning.

en.note: Word match, no inflection, so 'recorded' (a factual accounting verb) gives no warning.

added.term: allow: of record, record date, record dates
added.reason: Dividend terms ('shareholders of record'), not intensity.

added.term: records, significantly
added.reason: Forms of listed words, needed because this rule uses word match.
